conventions.convention: Forms and inner products are linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second; the energy norm is sqrt(a(v,v)).
The best-approximation gap is directed from the energy-unit sphere of E to the trial space; it is not a two-sided eigenspace gap.

Continuous eigenvalues start at index 1, increase with multiplicity, and diverge to positive infinity. The mass map is bounded, compact, injective and dense, and H is infinite-dimensional. Countable Choice is assumed.
Residual separation is measured from the real target parameter to the complementary eigenvalues, with zero included in the compact-operator spectral set.
The finite Hermitian directional estimate requires a specified simple target and positive separation from all other eigenvalues; residual proximity alone does not identify the lowest eigenvalue.
Cholesky whitening uses S=LL*, y=L*c and the Hermitian matrix L^{-1}HL^{-*}; it preserves the generalized pencil and Rayleigh quotient in exact arithmetic.

The conforming eigenvalue lower bound requires only sufficient trial-space dimension; the quadratic upper error requires a small directed energy gap. A coercive shift uses the shifted energy norm before subtracting the common spectral shift.
The Dirichlet examples retain both Choice and Countable Choice. Zero-boundary conformity is obtained for the real P1 hat on the matching eight-triangle square mesh.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, an infinite-dimensional Hilbert mass space, an injective bounded compact dense map J:V→H, and a bounded Hermitian coercive form a yield positive eigenvalues λ_j increasing with multiplicity to infinity, mass-orthonormal and energy-normalized eigenbases, the two Parseval expansions, and the attained identity λ_m=min_{dim S=m} max_{v∈S\{0}} a(v,v)/||Jv||².

Under Countable Choice, for a bounded Hermitian coercive form and finite-dimensional V_h⊆V, the unique energy projection P_h is linear and orthogonal, satisfies ||v−P_hv||_a=inf_{w_h∈V_h}||v−w_h||_a, and is injective on a nonzero finite-dimensional E if δ_a(E,V_h)<1.

Under Countable Choice, for an N-dimensional trial subspace with N≥1, bounded Hermitian coercive a and b(u,v)=(Ju,Jv) with bounded injective J, the positive increasing Ritz eigenvalues satisfy λ_{h,m}=min_{dim W_h=m} max_{v_h∈W_h\{0}} a(v_h,v_h)/b(v_h,v_h), for 1≤m≤N.

In the compact coercive form setting, if δ_h≤min{1/2,sqrt(λ_1/(6mλ_m))}, the projected energy-normalized first m directions form a basis, ||A_h−I||₂≤δ_h², ||B_h−D_m||₂≤(3m/λ_1)δ_h², and every nonzero vector in their projected span has quotient at most λ_m+(2λ_m+6mλ_m²/λ_1)δ_h².

In the compact coercive form setting, for dim V_h≥m there are δ_0>0 and finite C_m depending only on m and the first m continuous eigenvalues such that δ_h≤δ_0 implies λ_m≤λ_{h,m}≤λ_m+C_mδ_h². The lower bound needs no small-gap hypothesis; the shifted branch uses its shifted energy gap and subtracts the common shift.

Under Countable Choice, for compact self-adjoint B_h, a finite cluster Λ of nonzero eigenvalues with eigenspace sum F, and Δ=inf{|μ−ν|:ν∈Σ_h\Λ}>0, a residual bound ||(B_h−μI)u||≤ε||u|| on a nonzero finite-dimensional E implies gap(E,F)≤ε/Δ.
For finite Hermitian H and positive-definite S=LL*, the invertible change y=L*c makes Hc=λSc equivalent to (L^{-1}HL^{-*})y=λy and preserves the Rayleigh quotients.

seams_checked.note: Checked the mesh and broken/conforming definitions and the zero-boundary theorem against both square examples. The conforming example uses a real P1 hat on a finite matching mesh at p=2 with zero boundary traces and Countable Choice. No interpolation rate or mesh-family conclusion is imported.

Checked Céa, Galerkin orthogonality and Hermitian energy best approximation against the projection lemma. The datum a(v,·) is bounded and conjugate-linear, the trial space is finite-dimensional, and Countable Choice is retained. No Aubin–Nitsche regularity conclusion is used.

The incoming use in def-finite-basis-projector-energy-model assumes positive-definite S=LL*, uses h=L^{-1}h_0L^{-*} and y=L*c, and invokes exactly the supplier's preservation of the generalized Ritz quotient. Neither the definition nor its page imports a continuum bound or a finite-precision stability assertion.
